summary: I reviewed all requested files end to end, focusing on PII flow, success accounting, scheduler/state durability, and dashboard exposure paths. I found four P1 issues: one direct PII leak to logs, two false-success/wrong-person submission paths in the generic runner, and one setup path that recreates plaintext PII beside an encrypted config while silently leaving runtime on the old encrypted data.

findings.title: Raw form values are written to logs on select mismatches
findings.what: When a `<select>` field cannot match either by label or by value, the warning logs the exact submitted `value`. In this tool those values include name, email, state, zip, and country-derived fields.
findings.trigger: Any broker form with a select whose options do not exactly match the configured value, such as a renamed state/country selector or an international postal/region form.
findings.impact: User PII is emitted to stdout/stderr and can then land in run logs or the dashboard's live stream, violating the tool's primary privacy goal.
findings.fix: Do not log raw field contents. Log only the selector and a redacted field class, or redact all values before logging.

findings.title: Generic runner records success after only clicking a “Do Not Sell” link
findings.what: After `clickDoNotSell(page)` returns true, the code calls `fillGenericForm()` and `submitForm()` but ignores whether either actually succeeded, then unconditionally returns `finalize('Do Not Sell clicked')`. `runGenericBrokers()` later records that as success.
findings.trigger: A generic broker page with a visible “Do Not Sell” link/button that merely opens another page, modal, or form, but where no opt-out was actually submitted or toggled.
findings.impact: The tool reports the broker as removed and suppresses retries for 90 days even though no request may have left the machine.
findings.fix: Treat this path as success only if a concrete submit/preference-change signal is observed; otherwise return `manual` or a distinct non-success status.

findings.title: Generic broker submissions always use `persons[0]` and collapse state across people
findings.what: `activePerson()` hardcodes the first entry of `config.persons`, and the generic-runner skip/write paths key state by bare `broker.name` rather than `stateKey()`. In multi-person configs, later people do not get their own generic-broker submissions or state.
findings.trigger: A config using `persons` with more than one person, plus any generic broker flow that fills name/email fields.
findings.impact: One person's PII is sent during another person's run, and additional people can be marked skipped/removed without their own submission ever being made.
findings.fix: Pass the current person and total person count into the generic runner, derive field values from that person, and use `stateKey()` consistently for reads and writes.

findings.title: Rerunning setup on an encrypted install recreates plaintext config and leaves runtime on stale encrypted data
findings.what: Setup only loads existing plaintext `config.json`. If the installation already uses `config.json.enc`, setup starts from empty values, writes a fresh plaintext `config.json`, and only re-encrypts if the user explicitly opts in again. Meanwhile runtime still prefers `config.json.enc` in `loadConfig()`.
findings.trigger: User runs `node setup.js` after previously encrypting the config, intending to update PII, credentials, or schedule settings.
findings.impact: Full PII and secrets are written back to disk in plaintext, and the user's edits may be ignored at runtime because the tool continues loading the old encrypted config.
findings.fix: Make setup load through `loadConfig()`/`isConfigEncrypted()`, require the passphrase when editing an encrypted install, and rewrite the encrypted config in place instead of emitting plaintext by default.
